declared.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Mental Contrasting With Implementation Intentions on Goal Attainment
declared.foundIn: scout notes on Manson's ideas (idea 3); Crossref search « mental contrasting implementation intentions meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: 24 effect sizes from 21 field studies (15,907 participants, 87% of them in the 2 MOOC trials of Kizilcec 2017) of MCII against control

findings.text: Contrasting the goal with its obstacles and making if-then plans (MCII) helped people reach their goals more than control conditions

support.sentence: Results showed that MCII to be effective for goal attainment with a small to medium effect size (g = 0.336).

findings.text: The authors report publication bias: the real effect of MCII is probably smaller than 0.336

support.sentence: The results revealed that MCII is a brief and effective strategy for goal attainment with a small to moderate effect; however, because of some publication bias, the actual effect sizes may be smaller.

findings.text: The funnel plot was strongly asymmetric (Egger test p < .01); filling in 8 missing studies lowers the effect from 0.336 to 0.242

support.sentence: Finally, we used the “trim-and-fill” method to trim eight studies, and the adjusted values were 0.242, 95% CI (0.143, 0.342).
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle reviser, 2026-11-26: Europe PMC full text PMC8149892, Publication bias

findings.text: MCII guided by an experimenter worked better than MCII on paper or screen (moderator analysis without the 2 Kizilcec trials)

support.sentence: Specifically, studies with interventions based on interactions between participants and experimenters (g = 0.465) had stronger effects than studies with interventions based on interactions between participants and documents (g = 0.277).

limits: strong funnel asymmetry (Egger t = 5.46, p < .01); corrected by trim-and-fill only (8 studies added), no other bias model
87% of participants are in the 2 MOOC trials of Kizilcec 2017 (g = 0.09 and 0.06, intervals touching zero): not independent of kizilcec-2017-culture
13 of the 21 articles are co-authored by Oettingen or Gollwitzer, who created MCII; Oettingen was one of the article's reviewers
control conditions vary; few compare MCII with only dreaming about the goal
countries of the studies not listed; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
